subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must decide what a parameter must satisfy for a stated conclusion to hold
use when a parameter is solved for numerically although only a condition is required
anchor: A parameter condition is the requirement a coefficient must satisfy for the stated property to follow, which is usually an equation or inequality rather than a single value.
ordinary_language_bridge: Ask 'what would have to be true of this letter for the claim to hold?' rather than 'what number is it?'.
reconstruction_route: write the relation with the parameter kept symbolic
impose the stated property as an explicit condition
derive the constraint on the parameter from that condition
decide whether the constraint fixes a value, a set, or nothing
state the condition and say whether it is necessary, sufficient, or both

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same relation and the same imposed property
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: a condition that must hold versus a specific value that merely satisfies it
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Does any other value of the parameter also work?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: sufficiency requires checking the whole admissible set, not one example

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: any parameter question is answered by producing one number that works
misconception_discriminator.probe: ask whether a second candidate value also satisfies the stated property
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner reports the governing condition and its admissible set

repair_route: restore the parameter as a symbol
re-impose the stated property as an equation or inequality
re-derive the constraint and describe its solution set
retry on a case where the condition admits more than one value
verification_method: test one admissible and one inadmissible parameter value against the stated property
confirm the reported condition excludes the inadmissible value
known_limitations: does not cover parameters entering non-linearly without a separate treatment
does not establish that the stated property is well posed
